- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end of the range to avoid underestimating downside.  
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; apply a 3–5 day lag filter to smooth out short-term sentiment-driven overcorrections.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 2–4% to align with historical mean reversion.  
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is volatile (±0.5 or more in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to sentiment noise.
